insights.insight: 37,385 cryptographically confirmed receipts representing $2.58M in verified GMV establishes a deterministic purchase signal corpus — not modeled, not inferred — at a scale where category and brand patterns are statistically stable across rolling windows.

Probabilistic ad targeting pays $5+ CPM to infer purchase intent; a verified receipt confirms a transaction occurred, at a specific retailer, in a specific category — the gap between inference and proof is where this data asset sits.

insights.topic: Category mix reveals real consumer behavior
insights.insight: Grocery-supermarkets leads 14-day volume at 1,312 receipts ($61 average basket), with restaurants-dining, mass retail, and gas-convenience rounding out the footprint — a cross-category purchase graph built from ground truth, not panel estimates.

Walmart at 367 receipts, Costco at 162, Target at 118, Kroger at 76, and Home Depot at 72 over 14 days — brand-level confirmed purchase frequency, not share-of-voice or click attribution, with counts stable enough to track rolling-window churn.

Receipt accumulation has held at approximately 360–380 per day across the full monitoring window with no acceleration or decay, indicating a stable, repeatable data supply rather than burst-driven collection artifacts.

217 receipts in the Unknown category carry an average basket of $336 — roughly 5.5x the grocery average — suggesting a concentration of high-ticket verified spend that category resolution will unlock for targeting or measurement use cases.
